standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the support condition on A'/A into finiteness of its length.

standard_prerequisites.name: The element of the maximal ideal whose localization makes A and its normalization agree

core_obligations: Record that A' is a normal Nagata ring and that A -> A' is finite, using the Nagata hypothesis (proof lines 8301 onwards, at the start of the proof).

Choose f in the maximal ideal satisfying the equivalent conditions of the preceding lemma, so that A_f = A'_f, and conclude that the support of the finite A-module A'/A is contained in the maximal ideal (proof lines 8311-8312).
Apply the support-point lemma to conclude that A'/A has finite length as an A-module (proof lines 8313-8314).
proof_roadmap: Use the Nagata hypothesis for finiteness of the normalization.
Use the element f to confine the support of A'/A to the closed point.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the three properties of the integral closure A' of a reduced one-dimensional Nagata local ring A that make the delta-invariant well defined: A' is a normal Nagata ring, A -> A' is finite, and the quotient A'/A has finite length as an A-module. The finiteness of A -> A' is the Nagata hypothesis, and the length statement is obtained by choosing an element f of the maximal ideal satisfying the equivalent conditions of the preceding lemma, so that A_f equals A'_f; hence the support of the finite module A'/A is contained in the maximal ideal, and the module has finite length by the support-point lemma (proof lines 8301-8315). H2: the reduction of the length statement to the support of A'/A and the use of the element f are the substance, and the argument is short but complete.
